title: Zero Trust lab
summary: Keycloak and OpenZiti with tiered MFA and a deny-by-default firewall.

card.caption: Direct SSH by IP timed out; access only through the Ziti overlay.

kpis.label: roles, each with its own authentication tier

setup: A four-VM VirtualBox lab with a Keycloak realm and three roles. Each role has its own authentication tier: password, password plus TOTP, and password plus TOTP plus passkey.
did: Keycloak is wired into OpenZiti as an external JWT signer, so access follows identity groups rather than IP addresses, with separate dial and bind policies per service.
results: UFW denies by default. The apps are reachable only through the Ziti overlay, and a direct SSH attempt by IP from the same subnet timed out.
Identity-based authorization (Keycloak JWT + OpenZiti) removes application port exposure from the network.
failed: I documented a bind-policy misconfiguration that made clients act as service hosts instead of dialers.
next: Audit the separation of dial and bind policies so clients are not misconfigured as service hosts.
